title: We Also Serve
mainIdea: Animals have shown great courage and loyalty in helping people and deserve recognition for their service.

pages.text: Many animals have helped people during wars and emergencies through their hard work and loyalty.

question.text: Who are the main subjects of the story?

pages.text: Maria Dickin wanted to honor animals that showed courage while helping people.

question.text: Why did Maria Dickin want to honor the animals?
options: They were kept as pets in homes

pages.text: Animals faced dangerous situations while carrying messages, guiding people, and helping during emergencies.

question.text: What challenge did the animals face?
options: They could not find food during the long wars

pages.text: Pigeons delivered important messages, and guide dogs helped their owners reach safety during emergencies.

question.text: How did the animals help people?
options: By performing clever tricks for large crowds
By bravely carrying out important tasks

pages.text: Because of their courage and loyalty, many animals received the Dickin Medal, a special award for service.

options: The animals were forgotten once the wars had ended
The animals were honored with the Dickin Medal
The medal was removed and never given to animals

distractors: Farmers who raised animals for work
To keep all animals as pets
To sell trained animals to zoos

elements.correct: They faced danger during wars and emergencies
distractors: They needed long training before every mission
They carried loads that were too heavy to lift

elements.correct: They worked loyally and courageously to save lives
distractors: They performed clever tricks for cheering crowds
They guarded quiet farms far away from any danger

elements.correct: They were honored with the Dickin Medal
distractors: They were forgotten after the war ended
They were sent to live on quiet farms
